key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation and ANN models together can accurately predict weld temperature, axial force, and defect formation in HDPE friction stir welding, enabling fast identification of defect-free process windows.
engineering_relevance: The workflow provides a practical route to optimize thermoplastic weld quality by balancing rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating to reduce wormholes and stabilize welding forces.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model for thermal-mechanical welding simulation
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental data for temperature and axial-force prediction
Process-map generation across rotational speed, travel speed, and preheating conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong agreement with experiments, with reported R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL model matched observed void formation and thermal-mechanical behavior.
watch_item: The process map is based on a limited experimental parameter space, so broader validation is needed before generalizing to other HDPE grades, thicknesses, or tool geometries.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
